questions.stem: Which of the following defines the CEOI?
questions.key: A combat order that contains specific instructions for the operation of a particular communications system
distractors: A combat order that contains instructions explaining the use of the items included in the CEOI
A standing order that assigns communication responsibility to the commander
A signal annex listing motor and air messenger schedules
questions.explanation: The CEOI is a combat order with specific instructions for the operation of a particular communications system; it tells users what to do.
why: That defines the CESI, which tells users how to do the items in the CEOI.
Communication is the commander's responsibility, but that is not what defines the CEOI.
Messenger schedules are one section's content and may be moved to the signal annex of the command SOP.

questions.stem: It is a combat order that contains instructions explaining the use of the items that are included in the CEOI.
distractors: CEOI
Signal annex to the command SOP
CEOI extract
questions.explanation: The CESI tells the users how to do the items contained in the CEOI.
why: The CEOI tells users what to do.
The signal annex is a separate document that may carry messenger information.
A CEOI extract is the part of the CEOI taken forward to the command post.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the CESI as compared with the CEOI?
questions.key: Permanent in nature and prepared in only one edition
distractors: Prepared for short periods and subject to frequent change
Prepared in four editions to facilitate replacement upon compromise
Contains the specific instructions for operating a particular communications system
questions.explanation: The CESI is permanent in nature and prepared in only one edition, while the CEOI is prepared for short periods and subject to frequent change.
why: That describes the CEOI.
The four editions are a CEOI feature.
That is the CEOI's definition.

questions.stem: Which list gives the first four sections of the CEOI/CESI, in order?
questions.key: General, Messenger, Authentication, Code and Cipher
distractors: General, Authentication, Messenger, Code and Cipher
General, Messenger, Code and Cipher, Authentication
General, Messenger, Authentication, Radio
questions.explanation: The sections run 1 General, 2 Messenger, 3 Authentication, 4 Code and Cipher, 5 Radio, 6 Wire, 7 Visual and Sonic, 8 Information System.
why: Messenger is Section 2 and Authentication is Section 3.
Authentication is Section 3 and Code and Cipher is Section 4.
Radio is Section 5; the fourth section is Code and Cipher.

questions.stem: Which list contains the mandatory items of the General Section?
distractors: Index, Authentication, General Information
Distribution, Messenger schedules, General Information
Index, Distribution, Call signs
questions.explanation: The mandatory items in Section 1 are the Index, Distribution and General Information.
why: Authentication is its own section (Section 3).
Messenger schedules belong to Section 2 and may be omitted.
Call signs are Radio Section content (Section 5).

questions.stem: A section contains instructions on the type of radio to be operated, the station operating each net, call signs and frequencies. Which section is this?
distractors: Wire Section
Visual and Sonic System Section
Code and Cipher Section
questions.explanation: Section 5, the Radio Section (items 50-59), covers radio types, net stations, call signs, frequencies and radio relay.
why: The Wire Section covers the telephone directory, designators and wire tagging code.
The Visual and Sonic Section covers panel codes, recognition signals and pyrotechnic signals.
The Code and Cipher Section covers the codes and ciphers used to enhance communications security.

questions.stem: A section contains panel codes, recognition signals, air-to-ground recognition and pyrotechnic signals. Which section is this?
distractors: Wire Section
Information System Section
Authentication Section
questions.explanation: Section 7 holds instructions on sound and visual signals such as panel codes, recognition signals and pyrotechnic signals.
why: The Wire Section holds the telephone directory and designators.
The Information System Section holds email addresses and the data encryption key for computer transmission.
The Authentication Section holds the type of authentication used to protect against fraudulent reception or transmission.

questions.stem: A reserve edition has been prepared, published and issued to the using unit, but it is not in effect. Which CEOI edition is this?
distractors: 1st edition (basic edition)
3rd edition (Second Reserve)
4th edition (Third Reserve)
questions.explanation: The 2nd edition is the first reserve: issued to the using unit but not in effect.
why: The 1st edition is the effective edition.
The 3rd edition is not issued to the using unit and is kept in the issuing headquarters.
The 4th edition is a master copy or stencil kept in the preparing HQ's storage vault.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the 4th edition of the CEOI?
questions.key: Third Reserve, prepared by the issuing HQ as a master copy or in stencil form only and kept in its storage vault
distractors: Second Reserve, prepared and published but not issued to the using unit
Basic edition, prepared by the issuing HQ, issued to the using unit and in effect
First Reserve, prepared and issued to the using unit but not in effect
questions.explanation: The 4th edition is the third reserve, a master copy or stencil kept in the preparing headquarters' storage vault.
why: That defines the 3rd edition.
That defines the 1st edition.
That defines the 2nd edition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of the CEOI editions?
questions.key: The first edition and the first reserve should be stored together for quick replacement
distractors: The third edition is kept in the issuing headquarters
The fourth edition is a master copy kept in the preparing HQ's storage vault
The second edition is not in effect
questions.explanation: The first edition and the first reserve should never be stored in the same place, so one compromise does not expose both.
why: True: the 3rd edition is not issued to the using unit and is kept at the issuing headquarters.
True: the 4th edition is a master copy or stencil kept in the vault.
True: the 2nd edition is the first reserve and not in effect.

questions.stem: A CEOI is known to have been lost to unauthorized personnel. According to the lesson, what happens to the document?
questions.key: It is immediately pulled out of circulation and the first reserve is upgraded to the first or basic edition
distractors: It stays in use until the next scheduled edition cycle
It is reissued unchanged to the using unit with a new copy number
It is replaced by the third reserve issued directly to the using unit
questions.explanation: The four editions exist to facilitate replacement: on compromise, the document is pulled from circulation and the first reserve (2nd edition) becomes the basic edition.
why: A compromised document must be withdrawn immediately.
Changing only the copy number does not remove the compromise.
The replacement is the first reserve; the third reserve stays in the vault.

questions.stem: It is the term for a CEOI/CESI that is known or believed to have been captured, lost or exposed to unauthorized personnel, or misused so as to endanger the security of the communication-electronic system.
distractors: Short title
Copy number
Authentication
questions.explanation: The security slide defines compromise as known or believed capture, loss, exposure to unauthorized personnel, or misuse that endangers the C-E system.
why: A short title identifies a particular edition.
A copy number facilitates distribution, control and accounting.
Authentication protects the communication system from fraudulent reception or transmission.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines a short title?
questions.key: A combination of characters or a pronounceable word that identifies a particular edition of the CESI/CEOI
distractors: A number assigned to each copy to facilitate distribution, control and accounting
The number before the hyphen that identifies the specific item
The number after the hyphen that indicates the number of editions
questions.explanation: A short title provides brevity and added security and identifies a particular edition of the CESI/CEOI.
why: That defines the copy number.
That is the base number in the item number.
That is the edition number in the item number.

questions.stem: A compromise is discovered in a using unit. The Signal Officer submits an immediate report or spot report by the fastest means directly to whom?
distractors: The commander of the using unit only
G6/S6 of the next lower headquarters
Higher headquarters, by written report through command channels
questions.explanation: Page 18: the immediate or spot report goes by the fastest means direct to the G6/S6 of the issuing headquarters. The later written report goes through command channels.
why: The immediate report is not limited to the using unit's commander; it goes to the issuing HQ G6/S6.
The report goes to the issuing headquarters, not the next lower headquarters.
The written report that follows goes through command channels; the immediate report goes direct to the issuing HQ G6/S6.
